quote: I was just reading about y'all.
stewart_read: Customer opens with unsolicited high interest — a strong hook the rep never expands on.
coaching_implication: Rep should have asked 'what did you find interesting?' to build the emotional anchor before diving into qualification; instead this doubled as the skipped interest_question.

quote: We just like to be quick. So Yeah. I like that. I like that.
stewart_read: Rep acknowledges the customer's enthusiasm but pivots immediately to logistics instead of exploring it.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged the customer was already sold and didn't need further rapport-building.
coaching_implication: Even a fast-moving customer benefits from a 10-second interest probe — it becomes ammunition later when handling the shade objection.

quote: I do think that you don't have enough sun for solely for solar to work
stewart_read: Rep disqualifies the primary roof location based on Google Maps imagery alone, before customer has a chance to clarify actual sun exposure.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be legitimate: schema allows roof/shade hard DQ. But the abruptness before hearing the customer's counter-evidence is a process gap.
coaching_implication: Slow down the shade DQ — ask the customer to describe sun exposure directly rather than relying solely on satellite imagery before ruling it out.

quote: I was looking at we have a a detached garage. Is that possible to put it out there at the garage?
stewart_read: Customer proactively offers an alternative structure to make the deal work — a strong buying signal.
coaching_implication: This kind of customer-driven problem-solving is rare and valuable; should be routed to a specialist for an actual site visit rather than rep eyeballing Maps imagery.

quote: On the side, you have the other option is on the side of the house. There's no trees there.
stewart_read: Second alternative location offered unprompted by the customer — same motivated pattern.
coaching_implication: Two alternative-location offers in one call should trigger the rep to slow down and consider a specialist site assessment rather than a snap DQ from imagery.

quote: So for ground mounted systems, we don't offer them just because due to trenching and everything involved.
stewart_read: Rep gives a detailed cost/engineering rationale for why ground mounts aren't offered — closer-tier technical explanation delivered by the setter.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be a fast, honest DQ reason rather than scope creep, since it ends the pursuit rather than trying to sell.
coaching_implication: Even when disqualifying, avoid unpacking technical/cost rationale — a brief 'that's not something we do' keeps the setter in lane.
